clue.text: Taken in hand, like the coconut islands?

definitions.meaning: concealed in the hand, as a conjuror does with a card
planted with palm trees, as tropical coconut islands are

explanation.surface: A question about something grasped, likened to tropical isles of coconut trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: a conjuror's verb for hiding something in the hand, and an adjective for land covered in palm trees.

clue.text: He might appear in camera

indicators.note: might appear says the letters could show up in another form, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who could turn up in a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in camera' looks like photography or a private hearing; its letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: He stands for a man, here a citizen of the United States.

clue.text: Bully boys in the ring ?

parts.note: those who fight bulls in the bullring, rather than thugs

explanation.surface: Thugs in a boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bully boys' suggests ruffians; read as bull boys, they face bulls in the bullring.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullfighters who kill the bull in the arena.

clue.text: Destination of a dramatic consignment of wood

definitions.text: Destination of a dramatic consignment of wood

parts.words: Destination of a dramatic consignment of wood
parts.note: in Macbeth, Birnam Wood comes to the hill where Macbeth's castle stands

explanation.surface: Where a theatrical delivery of timber was sent.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Macbeth, soldiers carry branches from Birnam Wood to the castle hill, fulfilling the witches' prophecy.
explanation.definitionFit: The hill of Macbeth's castle, which the moving Birnam Wood reached.

clue.text: Poor Hook's caught by policeman in eating-house

indicators.note: caught by means held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a cop is a policeman

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, so the pirate's name is reworked into a new order

parts.note: the pirate's name with its s taken as written

explanation.surface: Captain Hook, down on his luck, is arrested by a constable in a cheap restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sees J. M. Barrie's pirate in trouble; 'Poor' is the anagram signal for his name, not pity.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a small restaurant or place selling cooked food.

clue.text: High rise buildings in 14

parts.note: lofty structures that exist only in a world of fantasy, the answer to 14

explanation.surface: Tower blocks in a place of fancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 down is DREAMLAND; idle hopes and fancies are buildings that exist only up in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for impractical daydreams, structures with no foundation.

clue.text: Jack up to his tricks again ?

definitions.text: Jack up to his tricks again

parts.words: Jack up to his tricks again
parts.note: a jack in cards is a knave, so his trickery is roguish behaviour

explanation.surface: A rogue named Jack misbehaving once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The jack in a pack of cards is also called the knave, and 'tricks' are also what card players win.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest roguish conduct, the behaviour of a rascal.

clue.text: But it shouldn't be difficult to sell

definitions.text: But it shouldn't be difficult to sell

parts.words: But it shouldn't be difficult to sell
parts.note: goods called hard should be no hard sell, a play on the two senses of difficult

explanation.surface: A salesman's paradox about stock that ought to move easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' is hard; the goods sold by ironmongers are called hard, though they should be easy to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: Tools and metal goods sold by an ironmonger, whose name contains a word for difficult.

clue.text: Sorry the camper's accommodation sounds so cheap

indicators.note: sounds means the phrase is to be heard as spoken rather than as written

parts.note: costing a penny, so very cheap
a camper sleeps under canvas, in a tent

explanation.surface: Regret that the camper's lodgings come across as so cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'penny tent', one costing a penny, said quickly: the coin's name blurs into the first syllables of the word for remorseful.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling remorse for wrongdoing, being repentant.

clue.text: Children unspoiled by these defeats

definitions.meaning: spare the rod and spoil the child: thrashings were once thought to stop children being spoilt
heavy losses, as a team takes when trounced

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned view of discipline: children kept from spoiling by these setbacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrashings given to children, and also the word for heavy losses in a contest.

clue.text: Her sisters tend to assist her

definitions.text: Her sisters tend to assist her

parts.words: Her sisters tend to assist her
parts.note: in a hospital the nursing sisters who tend patients work under the senior woman in charge

explanation.surface: A woman whose siblings tend to help her out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sisters' suggests family; in a British hospital a sister is a senior nurse, and they serve under the head of nursing.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional title of the senior nursing officer in a British hospital, to whom ward sisters report.

clue.text: Object of a quixotic charge

parts.note: Don Quixote famously charged at sails turning in the wind, taking them for giants

explanation.surface: The target of an impractically idealistic attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quixotic' usually means idealistic; here it points to Cervantes's knight literally tilting at giants that were really mills.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Quixote's lance-charge was at grain-grinding mills driven by sails, which he took for giants.

clue.text: Bird's cry, returning to it

indicators.note: returning means the word for cry is read backwards, coming back on itself

parts.note: to weep is to cry
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird's call that keeps coming back to the same note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns WEEP into PEEW; 'to' then adds IT. The name of the lapwing imitates its own call.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the lapwing, a plover of fields and moors named for its call.

clue.text: Epic means of musical transport

definitions.meaning: a portion of epic poetry suited to recitation in one go, as with Homer
a free, emotional musical composition; transport here means ecstasy

explanation.surface: A grand way of being carried away by music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like travel, but means rapture: a piece of music that carries the listener away.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a section of epic verse for recital, and an ecstatic free-form musical work.

clue.text: No real estate in this locality

definitions.text: No real estate in this locality

parts.words: No real estate in this locality
parts.note: a place that exists only in sleep has no real property at all

explanation.surface: An estate agent's note that there is no property in the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'real estate' suggests property; the point is that nothing in this realm is real, as it exists only in dreams.
explanation.definitionFit: An imaginary land of sleep and fantasy, where nothing is real.

clue.text: Conclusive evidence of unsupported legends

indicators.note: unsupported means without a leg to stand on, so a leg is taken away

explanation.surface: Proof that brings old tales to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsupported' removes LEG, a support, from LEGENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Conclusions or final portions are what close a thing, the concluding evidence of it.

clue.text: Coteries in secret assembly

indicators.note: assembly means putting together in a fresh arrangement, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Exclusive circles meeting in a clandestine gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' rearranges COTERIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Understood only by an inner circle, hence secret or obscure.

clue.text: Just a drop, but it could mean ruin

definitions.meaning: a fall of rain or snow, as from the sky
a collapse or fall from power

explanation.surface: Even a small fall could spell disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' suggests a small amount; it is the fall of rain or snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: a fall of rain or snow, and a loss of power or fortune.

clue.text: In Whitechapel they hide

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the run of letters of the next words

explanation.surface: Residents of an East End district keeping out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like a verb for the Whitechapel locals; it is a noun, an animal skin. Whitechapel is a district of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's skin with the fur on is called by both words.

clue.text: I report a rearrangement of capital

indicators.note: a rearrangement of means the letters that follow are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A journalist's claim of a reshuffle of money or a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rearrangement of' reorders I REPORT A.
explanation.definitionFit: The administrative capital city of South Africa.

clue.text: It may lay the foundation for a good score

definitions.text: It may lay the foundation for a good score

parts.words: It may lay the foundation for a good score
parts.note: an opera's text underlies the music the composer writes, the musical score

explanation.surface: Something that sets up a high total, as in sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' suggests points; it is the written music of an opera, which is set to words.
explanation.definitionFit: The text of an opera, on which the composer builds the music.

clue.text: Control of this Lapland transport sounds costly

parts.note: a rein is a means of control, as in keeping a tight rein

indicators.note: sounds means the next word is heard rather than read for its spelling

parts.note: dear means expensive

explanation.surface: Steering one of the Arctic sledge animals turns out to be expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The antlered animal that pulls sledges in Lapland, the far north of Scandinavia.

clue.text: To hurry goes against the grain in Cheshire

definitions.note: the definition reads as a place in Cheshire

indicators.note: goes against means is placed up against, next to the other piece

parts.note: to run is to hurry
corn is grain

explanation.surface: Rushing about seems contrary to one's nature in a northern county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes against the grain' looks like the idiom for something unnatural; it sets RUN beside CORN. Cheshire is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An industrial town on the Mersey estuary in the English county of Cheshire.

clue.text: This sort of right is given by letter

definitions.text: This sort of right is given by letter

parts.words: This sort of right is given by letter
parts.note: a letter here is one who lets property, and the person renting gains occupancy rights from them

explanation.surface: A kind of entitlement granted in writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' reads as correspondence; it means a landlord, one who lets.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rents from a landlord, holding rights to occupy the property.

clue.text: He's smart to confound the little beasts

indicators.note: to confound is to throw into confusion, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A clever fellow outwits some small creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to confound' rearranges the letters of HE'S SMART.
explanation.definitionFit: Small burrowing rodents kept as pets, fairly called little beasts.

clue.text: -Losing it is simply maddening

parts.note: to lose one's mind or sanity is literally to go mad

explanation.surface: A complaint that misplacing something drives you crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing it' seems a slang tantrum; taken literally, losing one's sanity is going mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The faculty of sane thought; losing it means going out of one's mind.

clue.text: Briskness, in City style ? 'Right in that

indicators.note: in means one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: a la is French for in the style of, so in City style is a la City

explanation.surface: A brisk manner, the way they do things in the Square Mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R into A LA CITY. The City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager quickness or briskness in acting.

clue.text: Newgate's was no list of saints

definitions.text: Newgate's was no list of saints

parts.words: Newgate's was no list of saints
parts.note: the Newgate record of notorious criminals was a register of villains, unlike a church list of saints' days

explanation.surface: The London prison's roll of inmates was hardly holy.
explanation.walkthrough: Newgate was a London prison; the Newgate Calendar was a famous record of its criminals, while a church version lists saints' days.
explanation.definitionFit: A church year lists saints' days; the Newgate one was a published register of notorious crimes.

clue.text: He got stuck, by George ! ,

parts.note: St George, England's patron saint, slew the beast by spearing it

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a man who became trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by George' sounds like an oath; it names the saint who speared the monster.
explanation.definitionFit: The fire-breathing monster that St George speared in the legend.
